drhp.business: SBL develops and manufactures a comprehensive range of friction products including drum brake linings, disc pads, clutch facings, and brake shoes for passenger, commercial, and two-wheeler vehicles. The company also produces lightweight engineered GFRP/CFRP composite structures for EV battery supports, drone components, and vehicle body parts. Its operations are supported by an in-house DSIR-recognized R&D center focused on material formulation, process optimization, and new product development for domestic and export markets.

risks.note: The Company was fined Rs. 3.28 Lakhs by NSE for non-compliance with board/committee composition requirements, experienced a five-day delay in filing financial results with BSE, and had a procedural lapse in disclosure format for the resignation of the Company Secretary/Compliance Officer. These incidents indicate vulnerability to administrative and procedural oversights that can lead to penalties and reputational impact.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk from stock-exchange listing obligations

risks.note: The Company Secretary, Compliance Officer, and Nodal Officer resigned effective 18 March 2026, and a replacement was appointed only on 25 May 2026. A gap in this critical governance role, combined with the disclosure lapse around the resignation itself, highlights exposure to disruption in regulatory filings and compliance continuity.
risks.risk: Key-person dependency and succession risk in compliance function

risks.note: As a focused manufacturer of brake linings, the Company's performance is structurally tied to the automotive OEM and aftermarket demand cycles. Any prolonged downturn in vehicle production or a shift in braking technology (e.g., regenerative braking in EVs) could materially reduce demand for its core friction-products.
risks.risk: Concentration of manufacturing and customer exposure to automotive cycles

risks.note: Brake-lining production depends on specialised friction materials, resins, and metals. Sustained input-cost inflation or disruption in the supply of key raw materials can compress margins, especially if the Company has limited ability to pass through costs quickly in competitive aftermarket and OEM segments.
risks.risk: Raw-material price volatility and supply-chain concentration

risks.note: The Company explicitly states it has no subsidiary, associate, or joint-venture companies. This single-entity structure concentrates all operational, financial, and strategic risk within one legal entity, leaving no diversification buffer across geographies, products, or business models.
risks.risk: Absence of subsidiary, JV, or associate diversification

risks.note: While the Board asserts adequacy of internal financial controls and the auditors reported no material fraud, the Company's risk-based internal audit plan and vigil mechanism have not been tested by any reported complaints. A false sense of security could delay detection if control weaknesses emerge in a lean governance structure.
risks.risk: Internal financial controls and fraud-detection reliance on audit processes
